newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--After reaching dizzying heights, the Athens Stock Exchange yesterday saw prices plunge six percent - the largest in one session. The panic selling followed warnings from the president of the Capital Market Commission on Wednesday. The government however attempted to put a brake on the selling, saying the rise on the ASE is normal and desirable.

--Announcing his candidacy for the post of conservative opposition leader, New Democracy deputy Kostas Karamanlis is now expected to make significant changes to the division of support between himself, president Miltiades Evert and former minister George Souflias.

--More tension in the Aegean as Turkish fighter planes infringe Greek air space: the new provocations came on the eve of the visit to Greece by NATO chief Javier Solana, who hopes to reduce tension between the two NATO allies.
--Drug-related deaths reached record levels in Greece last year, according to latest figures.
--A new interior ministry survey has shown civil servants would happily leave the embrace of the state if they could get a better-paying private sector job.
--Tax department officials have called the new E9 real estate declaration a "cryptic crossword" for taxpayers.
--The government has given striking teachers until Monday before any new meeting on demands. Reports add that the government has ruled out mobilising teachers to force them back to work.

--The New Democracy congress enters the final stretch with last night's declaration of candidacy by Karamanlis. Souflias has proposed a 13-point platform for the "renaissance" of the conservative party while Evert is preparing a rear-guard offensive.
--Some 100,000 property owners face fines if they do not declare their property to the National Land Register by deadlines. Fines can go up to 500,000 drachmas. ETHNOS
--Illegally-built homes must be declared on the E9 form, bringing these structures into the net of the tax department, the finance ministry hopes. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
